title: How should the Dayton DC meet peak-season throughput?
caption: IBIS deliberation map of the 2027 peak-capacity decision; 3 competing positions plus one framing sub-issue.

nodes.text: How should the Dayton DC meet 2027 peak throughput?
Is peak demand structural or a one-year spike?
Add a second shift with temp labor
Scales without a tight labor market
Wrong bet if demand is a one-year spike
Quality and safety dip with churn

semantic_description.level_1_elemental: An IBIS argument map: one root issue diamond, three competing position boxes, and one framing sub-issue, with pro and con argument nodes hanging off each position.
semantic_description.level_2_statistical: 14 nodes (2 questions, 3 ideas, 5 pros, 6 cons) and 13 typed edges. Each of the 3 positions carries at least one supporting and one objecting argument; the robotics position is the most contested (2 pros, 2 cons).
semantic_description.level_3_perceptual: The map reads as a balanced three-way deliberation rather than a settled answer: no position is argument-free, and the structural-vs-spike sub-issue branching off the root signals that the whole choice hinges on an unresolved framing question.
semantic_description.level_4_contextual: Surfaces that the capital-intensive robotics bet (I1) is only rational if peak demand is structural (Q2); the cheaper, reversible options (I2, I3) hedge the framing risk but trade away cost efficiency or SLA control.
semantic_description.short_alt: IBIS map: meeting 2027 peak DC throughput — three positions (robotics, second shift, 3PL) with pros and cons.
